qc_3_fairyland.blurb: Fairyland is a compact sector on the granite of Mont Rigaud in Quebec's Monteregie, set up and to the left of Bob's Wall. It holds eleven climbs, almost all of them bolted sport lines with one top-rope. Grades start around 5.6 and 5.7 and gather mostly in the 5.10s, with three routes reaching into the 5.11s, so it suits climbers who already lead steady 5.10. The wall faces southwest. This is a newer corner of the mountain, with routes added since 2016 and a few projects still unfinished. The way in is a faint trail with a couple of gaps to scramble through, less obvious than at the main walls.

qc_la_caverne.blurb: La Caverne is a small sector within the Guidou climbing area near Rouyn-Noranda, in Abitibi-Temiscamingue. It is a newer spot, described as a hidden gem with an atmosphere of its own. The eleven climbs are nearly all sport, plus one trad line, and the focus is steep, harder climbing: roughly half of the routes are 5.11 or 5.12, with a handful of 5.10s and only a couple of easier lines, including a multi-pitch 5.5 that reaches the top of the wall. Climbers can walk in from below along signed trails through the boulder field, or reach the top and rappel directly into the routes.

qc_le_dentiste.blurb: Le Dentiste is a small crag in the Guidou area outside Rouyn-Noranda, in Abitibi-Temiscamingue, slightly northeast of the main Boomtown wall. Short routes of roughly 10 to 13 metres are spread over three erratic boulders and one main wall, set in a narrow corridor with a distinctive feel. Of the eleven climbs, most are sport and a few are trad. Grades run widely, from easy 5.7 and 5.8 lines through a good block of 5.10s and 5.11s to a couple of 5.12 and 5.13 test pieces. The wall faces southwest, so it warms up earlier in the day than its neighbouring sectors. A well-marked trail of under a kilometre leads in.

qc_20_la_petite_folie.blurb: La Petite Folie is a small crag on Montagne d'Argent in the Laurentians, one of the many cliffs spread across the mountain. The rock offers a few short vertical cracks beside a low-angle slab, and the eleven climbs lean toward the easy end: six trad lines, four sport lines and one top-rope. Most routes sit around 5.4 to 5.6, with a few harder ones for climbers wanting a step up, and one two-pitch trad line. It makes a gentle spot for newer climbers learning to place gear or clip bolts. The walk from the welcome centre follows signs past the neighbouring Le Fou crag and is relatively flat and easy.

qc_le_gol.blurb: Le GOL is the largest and most remote of the cliffs at Attitude Montagne, in the Laurentians between Saint-Adolphe-d'Howard and Sainte-Agathe. It lies a little under a kilometre beyond the Amphithéâtre sector, reached by taking the left fork and following the trail, while the site's other cliffs are all within about ten minutes of the parking. Described as a very quiet sector facing west, it holds eleven climbs, a mix of sport and trad with some top-rope. Grades run from about 5.7 up to the low 5.11s, with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.9, which suits climbers wanting moderate routes away from the busier walls.
